integrated_multimodal_description:
Single-take constraint: exactly one continuous shot from first frame to last frame. No cuts, shot switches, jump cuts, dissolves, wipes, fade transitions, hidden cuts behind occlusion, abrupt viewpoint resets or scene morphing. All framing changes must result from a visible continuous camera path, with coherent intermediate views, parallax and lighting. Action-speed ramps do not interrupt the take.

Action speed: 0.00–1.20 seconds at natural real-time speed for the glance and door opening; 1.20–2.40 seconds is a quick, sharp real-time stumble and release, not slow motion; 2.40–2.80 seconds smoothly decelerates into pronounced slow motion; 2.80–4.00 seconds sustains pronounced slow motion for the airborne props and spreading arms. Camera speed stays slow and steady throughout, independent of the action-speed ramp.

[Shot 1] Photorealistic live-action office elevator scene. Start with the exact first-frame composition: the woman holds the orange phone and lidded paper coffee cup, wearing her navy badge lanyard. During 0.00–1.20 seconds she glances toward the elevator as its doors open. During 1.20–2.40 seconds she takes a short step, abruptly checks her movement and recoils, opening her hands involuntarily. The phone and cup leave her hands; the loose lanyard slips over her bowed head and swings outward as one connected badge-and-strap object. During 2.40–4.00 seconds smoothly ramp into high-speed slow motion: she spreads her arms, tracks the phone with startled eyes, and the three objects continue moving along short inertial arcs, arriving at the exact last-frame positions. The camera makes a modest forward dolly at a steady slow speed toward the open elevator. Maintain her identity, coral blouse, black suit and skirt, realistic skin and cloth, and exactly one of each prop. No dialogue, graphic overlays, arrows, skeletal effects, glow, duplicated objects or object teleportation.

overall_soundscape:
Quiet lobby ventilation, a single elevator chime as the doors open, a brief heel scuff and fabric rustle at the stumble. No impact suggesting that a prop has already hit the floor.
